Title: Fatal crash that killed four happened when car went out of control
Article:
GERIK: The crash on the Gerak-Jeli stretch of the East-West Highway that killed four, including a child, happened when the Perodua Axia they were travelling in went out of control.
The vehicle entered the opposite lane at Km38.5 of the highway near Tasik Banding and crashed into another car and a lorry.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the Axia was travelling from Gerik towards Jeli when the crash happened about 1.30pm.
He said the vehicle crashed into the rear of a Proton Persona, which was travelling from Jeli towards Gerik.
"Following the
collision
, the Axia went underneath the lorry and was dragged for about 3m to 7m,"  he said in a statement.
Alwi said four occupants of the Axia, comprising two men, a woman and a child, were confirmed dead.
"Another child suffered serious injuries and was taken to Gerik Hospital for treatment.
"The Axia was driven by a 19-year-old man and had four passengers comprising a 31-year-old man, a 40-year-old woman and two children.
"The Proton Persona was driven by a 20-year-old man with three passengers – two men aged 19 and 47, and a 47-year-old woman," he said.
He added that the lorry was driven by a 42-year-old man and had a 34-year-old male attendant.
Alwi said the Proton Persona driver and all its passengers, as well as the lorry driver and attendant, were uninjured.
"All three vehicles involved will be sent for technical inspection.
"Police are also tracing independent witnesses and seeking closed-circuit television (CCTV) and dashboard camera (dashcam) recordings, if available, to assist further investigations," he said.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Those with information on the crash are urged to come forward to assist with investigations.
Meanwhile, the identities of the victims have been established, but their relationship has yet to be ascertained.
Gerik police chief Superintendent Abdul Samad Othman said the victims were all from Kota Baru.
They were identified as Al Zubair Deraman, 31; Tuan Shazrin Tuan Mud, 40; and Nik Mohamad Hafiz Daniel Nik Hairey, 19.
He said the identity of the child, a girl, had yet to be ascertained.
The injured victim was identified as Mohammad Shiraz Hammani Abdul Fattah, 9.

Title: Kelantan authorities captured 36 stray dogs, including where boy, 8, was mauled
Article:
KOTA BARU: Local councils in the state have captured 36 stray dogs this year, with most of the animals rounded up in Bachok, including the Kemasin area where an 8-year-old boy was recently attacked.
State Local Government, Housing, Health and Environment Committee chairman Hilmi Abdullah said the operations were carried out between January and last week.
"The local authorities had intensified efforts to address the stray dog problem, particularly in areas where such animals had been reported to pose a threat to the public.
"As of October, 36 stray dogs have been captured.
"Most of them were caught in Bachok, including Kemasin and other surrounding areas.
"Some of the dogs were captured while the rest had entered the traps," he said.
The 8-year-old boy was injured after being attacked by more than five stray dogs while playing at Pantai Kuala Kemasin in Bachok on Thursday.
The boy sustained injuries to his head, neck and hand in the incident and underwent surgery to treat his wounds.
It was reported today that the
boy will also be given anti-rabies
injections to prevent infection.
His mother, Rosnani Mat Salleh, 46, said the vaccination was part of a multi-week follow-up treatment plan for her son, Azuar Firdaus Zuraiman, following a five-hour surgery yesterday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Yong Peng schoolgirl murder: Victim buried in Batu Pahat
Article:
BATU PAHAT: The Form Four pupil who was believed to have been murdered at a school in Yong Peng was laid to rest at the Kampung Parit Arshad Muslim cemetery, here.
The body of Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal arrived at her grandmother's house in Kampung Parit Selamat, Yong Peng, at 6.30pm after a post-mortem examination at Sultanah Nora Ismail Hospital (HSNI) here.
The funeral prayers for the girl were performed at her grandmother's house and at the Kampung Parit Arshad mosque, attended by more than 100 congregants made up of relatives, acquaintances and villagers.
Many were unable to hold back their tears as the body was brought into her grandmother's house on its final journey before burial.
Earlier, the
16-year-old suspect who was detained
at 7pm yesterday was remanded for six days by the Batu Pahat magistrate's court.
Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said in a statement police had seized a mobile phone, a set of clothing and slippers following the suspect's arrest.
He said the suspect was detained by a team of Johor Criminal Investigation Department policemen, aided by a team from the Batu Pahat CID, a few hours after the incident.
"The suspect was detained around Yong Peng after police received information about the discovery of the victim, who was unconscious and covered in blood.
"The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mercedes-AMG brings V8, electric firepower as F1 returns to Malaysia
Article:
MERCEDES-Benz Malaysia has brought two very different interpretations of high-performance motoring to the local market with the new Mercedes-AMG GT 63 Pro 4Matic+ Coupé and a preview of the all-new AMG GT 63 four-door coupé.
Unveiled as Formula 1 returns to Malaysia this week, the two models showcase AMG's approach to performance at opposite ends of the powertrain spectrum - one centred on a 4.0-litre V8 biturbo engine and the other on an all-electric AMG.EA architecture.
The GT 63 Pro 4Matic+ Coupé is priced from an estimated RM2.09 million in Peninsular Malaysia, while the limited Motorsport Collectors Edition is priced at RM2.59 million.
Mercedes-Benz Cars Malaysia chief executive officer and president, and head of region for Mercedes-Benz Cars Southeast Asia Martin Schulz said the two models reflected AMG's focus on combining performance with emotion.
"The new Mercedes-AMG GT 63 Pro 4Matic+ Coupé brings the thrill of motorsport to the road … while the all-new Mercedes-AMG GT 63 four-door coupé shows how that same spirit can be reimagined for the electric era," he said.
V8 Power, Track-Focused Hardware
The GT 63 Pro is powered by AMG's 4.0-litre V8 biturbo engine producing 450 kW, or 612 hp, and 850 Nm of torque.
That represents a 20 kW increase in output and 50 Nm more torque than the standard AMG GT 63.
Power is sent through AMG's Speedshift MCT 9G transmission and fully variable AMG Performance 4Matic+ all-wheel drive.
The coupé can accelerate from zero to 100 km/h in 3.2 seconds and reach a top speed of 317 km/h. It takes just 10.9 seconds to reach 200 km/h.
AMG has also concentrated on keeping the car cool under sustained track use.
The cooling package has been expanded with additional radiators positioned in the front wheel arches, while the differentials and transfer case also receive active cooling.
Revised underbody air guides and brake cooling ducts help direct more air towards the braking system.
More Grip, Less Lift
The GT 63 Pro also gets extensive aerodynamic changes designed to improve stability and steering precision at high speeds.
Its redesigned front apron features carbon-fibre air deflectors, while active aerodynamic elements in the underbody work with an Airpanel system and a fixed rear wing.
Mercedes-AMG says these changes reduce front-axle aerodynamic lift by more than 30kg, while the rear wing increases rear-axle downforce by about 15kg.
The car rides on AMG Active Ride Control suspension with active roll stabilisation, while rear-axle steering can provide up to 2.5 degrees of steering angle.
Braking duties are handled by AMG ceramic high-performance composite brakes with 420mm discs and six-piston fixed callipers at the front.
The package is designed to withstand repeated heavy braking while reducing unsprung weight.
Carbon-Fibre ameets Luxury
Inside, the GT 63 Pro combines motorsport-inspired equipment with luxury-car technology.
The cabin features AMG Performance seats in Nappa leather and Microcut microfibre, a carbon-fibre/Microcut steering wheel, carbon-fibre trim and yellow seat belts.
A 12.3-inch driver display sits alongside an 11.9-inch central display, with a head-up display and augmented-reality navigation.
AMG Track Pace provides lap, sector and acceleration data for closed-course driving, while the equipment list also includes the Energising Package, Thermotronic automatic climate control and Burmester surround sound.
200 Units Limit
For collectors, Mercedes-AMG is offering a Motorsport Collectors Edition limited to just 200 units globally.
Based on the GT 63 Pro, the special edition features an Obsidian Black finish with Mercedes-Benz Star Pattern graphics and Petronas-coloured exterior accents inspired by Formula 1.
It also features 21-inch forged wheels, carbon-fibre and AMG Night Package elements, Petronas-accented brake callipers and an AMG aerodynamic package.
The cabin receives matching Petronas detailing, AMG Performance seats, carbon-fibre trim and an edition-specific centre-console badge.
The model also comes with a Burmester high-end 3D surround sound system and the Energising Plus Package.
AMG's Electric Flagship
While the GT 63 Pro celebrates the V8, the all-new AMG GT 63 four-door coupé points to the brand's electric future.
The four-door model is based on AMG.EA, a dedicated high-performance electric vehicle architecture, and uses three axial-flux electric motors.
Combined output is up to 860 kW, or 1,169 hp.
The drivetrain is paired with AMG's high performance electric battery, which uses cylindrical cells with direct cooling and an 800-volt electrical architecture.
The setup is designed not only to deliver high peak output but also to sustain performance under repeated high-load conditions.
The car supports DC charging of up to 350 kW, with battery pre-conditioning and thermal management designed to maintain charging performance.
Simulated V8, Electric Performance
AMG has also taken an unusual approach to the electric car's sound and driving character.
Its AMGForce S+ drive programme is designed to provide a V8-inspired experience through simulated gear shifts, sounds and driver-display changes.
The system uses more than 1,600 sound files to create a dynamic acoustic experience that responds to acceleration, gear-change simulations and other driving inputs.
Underneath, the AMG Race Engineer system integrates control of the powertrain, charging, energy management and driving dynamics.
Three rotary controls allow the driver to adjust response, agility and traction characteristics.
The traction control system offers nine levels of adjustment in the appropriate performance modes.
Built For Corners
The GT 63 four-door coupé gets AMG Active Ride Control air suspension with semi-active roll stabilisation, while multi-link front and rear axles maintain wheel control during high-speed cornering.
Active rear-axle steering can turn the rear wheels in the opposite direction to the front wheels at lower speeds to improve agility.
Above 80 km/h, the rear wheels turn in the same direction as the front wheels to improve high-speed stability.
AMG Performance 4Matic+ all-wheel drive provides continuously variable torque distribution between the front and rear axles, with torque vectoring between the rear wheels.
Performance Meets Everyday Use
Despite its performance focus, the four-door model is designed to retain the practicality expected of a grand tourer.
The cabin features AMG Performance seats, Nappa leather and Microcut upholstery, carbon-fibre trim and a panoramic Sky Control roof.
The dashboard combines a 10.2-inch instrument cluster with a 14-inch central display, while the front passenger gets a separate 14-inch screen.
Other equipment includes smartphone integration, augmented-reality navigation and a selfie and video camera.
The two cars offer markedly different routes to AMG performance - the GT 63 Pro leaning heavily on traditional V8 power and track-focused hardware, while the GT 63 four-door coupé demonstrates how AMG is translating its performance philosophy into the electric era.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Brazil votes in nail-biter polls closely watched by Trump
Article:
BRASÍLIA: Brazilians headed to the polls on Sunday in a toss-up race between President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Flavio Bolsonaro that will decide whether Latin America's biggest nation follows a regional swing to the right championed by US President Donald Trump.
From villages deep in the Amazon rainforest to the agricultural heartlands in the south and sprawling urban favelas, Brazilians are facing a familiar cast – with many forced to pick who they least dislike.
Soon to turn 81 years old, the veteran leftist Lula is seeking a fourth and final term in office, warning voters that Brazil's sovereignty is at stake due to pressure from Trump.
He is facing a tough battle from right-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro, 45, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year sentence for attempting a coup after his failed 2022 re-election bid.
Opinion polls show neither candidate is likely to reach more than the 50 percent threshold required to win in the first round on Sunday, putting them neck-and-neck in an October 25 runoff.
Lula has an advantage in Brazil's poor northeast, and among low-income voters, Catholics, and women.
"I am very worried because I want a victory. I can't understand poor people who are right-wing, because we are naturally left-wing people," Maria de Nazare Azevedo, a 57-year-old civil servant, told AFP.
"We are poor, we are Northeasterners. Poor right-wingers drive me crazy," said Azevedo, who lives in Rio de Janeiro but hails from the Amazonian city of Belem.
Bolsonaro leads in the south, among wealthier voters and evangelicals.
"What we need is change, to change politics, to change our security situation. There have been a lot of robberies where I work, and I've witnessed various incidents," said Bolsonaro supporter Babiliana Figueira, 40, a civilian firefighter.
Both candidates have extremely high rejection rates in the deeply polarized nation where a bitter election campaign featured more scandals and mud-slinging than policy and promises.
Lula has slammed Bolsonaro as a "nobody" who is "not even fit to be a building manager."
Bolsonaro, who has cast himself as more "moderate" said Brazilians "can't stand" Lula anymore.
- 'MORE ENEMIES' -
Lula, revered for social welfare programs that lifted millions out of poverty, made a dramatic comeback to office in the 2022 elections after a massive corruption scandal that saw him jailed for over 18 months.
The charges, thrown out on procedural grounds, have continued to haunt him.
He beat Jair Bolsonaro in 2022 by only 1.8 percentage points.
Riots in Brasilia and the botched coup attempt after his election allowed him to cast himself as guardian of Brazil's democracy, even as Jair Bolsonaro's trial and conviction only deepened divisions.
In his third term he has overseen a drop in inflation and unemployment, but voters complain about a high cost of living and are fed up with crime.
Lula has also sharply curbed deforestation in the Amazon, but the environment has barely registered as a campaign issue.
Indigenous chief Bepdjo Mekragnotire, 45, of the Bau village in the Amazon, told AFP ahead of the vote: "We stand with Lula, all of us."
"Our concern is that if Flavio wins, there will be more enemies – more illegal mining, more logging," he said.
- THE TRUMP FACTOR -
Trump has loomed large over the campaign, and said he is "very closely" watching the election, but he has not endorsed Flavio Bolsonaro.
The US president has wielded tariffs and sanctions to pressure Brasilia over complaints ranging from the trial against his ally Jair Bolsonaro to alleged unfair trade practices.
Lula has repeatedly warned him not to "meddle" in the elections.
Flavio Bolsonaro's rallies have featured massive US flags and images of Trump.
Buoyed by his father's legacy, he has been a formidable rival for Lula, even as it emerged that he was under investigation for corruption over the financing of the biopic "Dark Horse" about his father.
The younger Bolsonaro has vowed a hardline approach to crime and fiscal austerity amid rising public debt.
Carlos Roberto dos Santos, 62, a cattle rancher in the southeastern city of Barretos who supports Bolsonaro, told AFP he was fed up with unchecked government spending.
"They have so many social programs. To pay off the debt they have to raise interest rates and create new taxes. That affects every sector, not just agriculture."--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UiTM difficulties must push institution to improve, says Zambry
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) must use the challenges it faces as a catalyst to improve rather than allow them to undermine the institution.
Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said weaknesses within the university must be addressed openly, with efforts focused on strengthening the institution and ensuring its graduates become nation builders.
"There are shortcomings and weaknesses — we will improve them. We will not simply allow these weaknesses to remain just because we want to cover them up.
"We will not do that. Instead, our commitment is to do our very best to restore and strengthen the institution," he said at the Wacana Semarak Patriotisme Seminar Ilmuwan Islam at UiTM Shah Alam.
UiTM has come under scrutiny after a former UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd group chief executive officer was charged with
criminal breach of trust
involving RM37.37 million.
UiTM Holdings previously recorded accumulated pre-tax losses of about RM157 million for the 2017, 2018, 2019 and 2021 financial years.
The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission launched an investigation in 2023 into alleged misappropriation involving the company, including a 50-megawatt solar project in Gambang, Pahang.
MACC has since identified
governance lapses
in UiTM Holdings and recommended improvements, with Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman saying such recommendations were standard when investigations uncovered governance weaknesses.
Zambry said UiTM remained an important institution and had produced more than a million graduates since its beginnings as the Rural and Industrial Development Authority (Rida) Training Centre.
"UiTM is a very meaningful institution, steeped in the history of the Malay people's struggle.
"What began as a Rida Training Centre is today known as UiTM, and it has produced more than one million graduates. How will those who graduate from UiTM become nation builders?
"Our first objective is to become knowledge seekers. When knowledge reaches us, its meaning becomes part of us. When that meaning becomes part of us, it shapes who we are, our character and our manners," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid proposes quantum technology department at UiTM by next year
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi wants Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) to establish a quantum technology department by next year to produce specialists in the emerging field.
The deputy prime minister said the move would help ensure Malaysia keeps pace with developed countries in quantum technology.
"I hope a quantum department can be established at UiTM, which could eventually grow into a faculty.
"This is a new technology that will put our country at the forefront, alongside other developed nations.
"Artificial intelligence is good and we have done very well in that field, but quantum is a new technology based on the latest technological developments. Malaysia should not be left behind," he told reporters after opening the Wacana Semarak Patriotisme Seminar Ilmuwan Islam at UiTM Shah Alam.
Present were Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir, Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki and UiTM Board of Directors chairman Tan Sri Mohd Khamil Jamil.
Zahid said RM500,000 would be allocated to UiTM as initial funding to kick-start the proposed department.
"I am confident there is tremendous potential to attract many students into this field, and that within less than a decade, we will be able to produce quantum specialists in the country.
"I leave it to Tan Sri Khamil to determine how the allocation will be used. This is merely the initial funding that I will provide so that steps to establish the department can begin immediately," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] BN to announce Melaka election partners after Oct 7
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Barisan Nasional will announce its choice of partners for the Melaka election after the Election Commission's announcement on Oct 7, its chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said.
He said BN had held discussions with other parties but had yet to make a decision.
"We will wait for the Election Commission's announcement on Oct 7. After that, there will be an announcement on which coalition we should prioritise working with or reach an understanding with to contest the Melaka election," he told reporters after opening the Wacana Semarak Patriotisme Seminar Ilmuwan Islam here today.
The EC is scheduled to hold a
special meeting
on Oct 7 to determine key election dates, including nomination and polling days, following the dissolution of the Melaka state assembly.
BN has been weighing cooperation with Pakatan Harapan or Perikatan Nasional, or contesting on its own.
Meanwhile, Zahid said BN had drawn up plans to mobilise its election machinery and build a "blue wave" in Melaka.
"We are planning to mobilise the machinery so that the blue wave in Melaka can truly take shape and eventually spread across the country when the time comes," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BN open to Pas using its logo in Melaka, but no decision yet
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Barisan Nasional is open to Pas using the BN logo if they cooperate in the Melaka election, but no decision has been made, said coalition chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
"The matter has not been formally discussed. But I believe that if Pas contests, they would be more comfortable using their own logo, as they did in the Johor and Negri Sembilan elections.
"We have no problem if they want to use the logo they propose. That is a matter for their party," he told reporters after opening the Wacana Semarak Patriotisme Seminar Ilmuwan Islam here today.
Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi had previously said
his party was open
to using the BN logo in the Melaka election should there be cooperation with the coalition.
The question over which logo Pas could use comes amid the suspension of Perikatan Nasional activities.
On Sept 23, the Registrar of Societies (RoS)
suspended all PN activities
under Subsection 13(2A) of the Societies Act 1966.
The suspension followed a notice issued a day earlier requiring PN to explain a complaint lodged by Bersatu with the RoS.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BN still open to cooperation with PH in Melaka
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Barisan Nasional is still open to working with Pakatan Harapan in the Melaka election, says its chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
He said BN had held discussions with other parties and rated the progress of those talks at "9.5" on a scale of one to 10.
"We are very open," he told reporters after opening the Wacana Semarak Patriotisme Seminar Ilmuwan Islam here.
He said this when asked whether BN was still willing to discuss cooperation with PH.
BN has been weighing cooperation with either PH or Perikatan Nasional (PN), or contesting on its own, following the dissolution of the Melaka state assembly.
On Tuesday, Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said the
coalition would take its cue
from the PH presidential council's official decision rather than Amanah communications director Khalid Abdul Samad's remarks on electoral cooperation.
He said individual statements did not reflect PH's overall position, adding that BN would await developments following a formal invitation for talks on a possible political understanding.
Khalid had said that PH would not cooperate with BN in the Melaka election, claiming the coalition had already decided on the matter and was open to working with any party except BN and PN.
Meanwhile, Zahid said BN's grassroots machinery would work alongside its eventual coalition partner throughout the campaign for the 16th Melaka state election.
"At the grassroots level, particularly at the polling district centres, our machinery will work together even though we have yet to decide which partner we will work with.
"But we are planning to mobilise the machinery so that the blue wave in Melaka can truly take shape and eventually spread across the country when the time comes," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Putrajaya Line resumes normal operations after cable theft
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Putrajaya MRT Line resumed normal operations at 1.27pm today after repair works following a cable theft incident near Taman Equine Station were completed.
Rapid KL said the restoration of power supply allowed trains, which had previously been disrupted at Taman Equine Station, to resume normal operations.
Alternative train services provided during the disruption have been discontinued, while train frequency is being progressively adjusted to ensure stable operations.
"During this period, shuttle bus services will continue to be provided until 3pm.
"The service will be reassessed based on operational requirements at the time," Rapid KL said in a statement today.
Repair works on the affected cables will continue tonight during engineering hours to complete the infrastructure restoration.
Rapid KL said it was also cooperating with the authorities in investigations into the
cable theft
.
The operator apologised for the inconvenience caused to passengers during the disruption and thanked them for their patience and cooperation.
Passengers have been advised to obtain the latest service updates through Rapid KL's social media channels and the MyRapid PULSE travel application.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Water in RON95 tank claim: Checks find no contamination at petrol station
Article:
BATU KAWAN: The Penang Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry has found no evidence of water contamination in RON95 storage tanks at a Batu Kawan petrol station following a viral complaint.
State ministry director S. Jegan said inspections were conducted jointly with the oil company and station operator after a social media post alleged vehicle problems following refuelling.
He said checks of the station's Automatic Tank Gauge (ATG) records showed no indication of water in the RON95 tank during the inspection or the preceding three days.
He said physical inspections of the pump area and tank sump also found no water accumulation apart from normal condensation.
Manual dipping tests were conducted on both RON95 tanks using Water Finding Paste (WFP), which changes colour when water is detected.
"No colour change was observed, indicating no presence of water in the tanks.
"Fuel discharged from all pump nozzles is also visually inspected and found to be clear, with no visible signs of contamination," said Jegan.
He said the ministry, the oil company and station operator would continue working together to address the matter and safeguard consumers.
"Consumers' interests and safety will always be given priority," he added.
Jegan urged the public not to jump to conclusions based on information circulating on social media and to submit any related complaints directly to the ministry.
Several posts had gone viral on social media alleging that vehicles experienced problems, including being unable to start, after refuelling at several petrol stations around Penang.
The posts also claimed that the problem was suspected to have been caused by water-contaminated fuel.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Eight areas record unhealthy air quality
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Eight areas across Johor, Negri Sembilan and Sarawak recorded unhealthy air quality as of 5pm.
Data from the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) showed Segamat and Batu Pahat in Johor recording the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at 155, followed by Kluang at 152, Tangkak at 151 and Larkin at 111.
In Negri Sembilan, Nilai recorded an API reading of 146 and Seremban 139, while Samarahan in Sarawak recorded 119.
Another 57 air quality monitoring stations nationwide registered moderate API levels, including Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur, Bukit Rambai in Melaka, Putrajaya, Banting in Selangor, Kemaman in Terengganu, Temerloh in Pahang, Pegoh Ipoh in Perak, Sungai Petani in Kedah, Kota Bharu in Kelantan and Balik Pulau in Penang.
Only three areas recorded good air quality: Sandakan, Kangar and Langkawi.
API readings of zero to 50 are classified as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy and above 300 as hazardous.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man dies after suspected electric shock while stealing cable
Article:
SHAH ALAM: A man died after he was believed to have been electrocuted while stealing a Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) cable along Jalan Acob, Kapar, Klang, about 10am today.
Klang Utara police chief Assistant Commissioner Ramsay Embol said police were alerted by a member of the public who found the man's body at the scene.
"Initial investigations found that the man, believed to be in his 40s, was electrocuted while stealing the cable, with his hand still attached to it.
"Police also found cable-cutting equipment and a motorcycle believed to have been used by the man at the scene," he said in a statement.
He said the man, who was from Kapar, was later identified by his family, and the case was classified as sudden death.
The body was taken to Al-Sultan Abdullah Hospital, UiTM Puncak Alam, for post-mortem examination.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Don't let Melaka election rivalry affect national stability, says Johari
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Political parties must not allow rivalry in the Melaka election to turn into quarrels that could undermine national stability, says Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.
"The most important thing is that this is politics. It is not about fighting. The country must be stable," he told reporters when asked for updates on election preparations and seat negotiations.
Speaking after attending the Raintree Invitational tennis tournament at the Raintree Club Kuala Lumpur, Johari said stability was essential for economic growth and investor confidence.
"When the country is stable, the economy can move and investors can come.
"Those who have come do not want to leave, and those who have not will come because they see Malaysia as a very mature country politically," he said, adding that Malaysia had changed prime ministers several times without political upheaval.
"We want stability. You can do anything you want to do, but we have to maintain that democracy," he said.
Johari said political alliances could shift, but rivals must maintain order.
"Today you are with one party, tomorrow you are with another, and the day after you come back to that party. That is it. It is politics," he said.
Johari, who is also Titiwangsa member of parliament, said club officials had invited him to help revive the tournament after a 13-year hiatus.
He urged the club to continue organising the event to nurture young talent and pledged RM10,000 for future editions.
The Election Commission has yet to announce the nomination and polling dates for the Melaka election following the dissolution of the state assembly on Sept 23.
In the last
state election
, Barisan Nasional (BN) won 21 of the 28 seats, Pakatan Harapan secured five and Perikatan Nasional (PN) won two.
BN is in talks with PN, with negotiations reportedly in the final stage.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Senior citizen loses RM113,550 in phone scam
Article:
JERANTUT: A senior citizen lost RM113,550 to a phone scam last month after a caller posing as a police officer told him he was involved in money laundering.
The 69-year-old victim, who panicked after being told he was involved in the illicit activity, withdrew money from automated teller machines (ATMs) before depositing it into unknown bank accounts.
Jerantut police chief Superintendent Noor Azman Yusof said the victim received a phone call from someone posing as a policeman on Sept 11.
"The caller told the victim that he was involved in money laundering activities. The victim chose not to inform his children about the allegations.
"He withdrew a total of RM113,550 on 20 occasions via ATMs at two banks in Jerantut and Jengka between Sept 11 and yesterday before depositing the money into unknown bank accounts," he said.
Noor Azman said the victim only realised that he had been cheated after telling his children about the allegations. He lodged a police report yesterday.
He advised the public not to panic or fall for calls from unknown numbers claiming that they were involved in criminal cases or threatening them with legal action.
The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar: Malaysia discussing F1 returning to Sepang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government is actively discussing the possibility of having Malaysia back on the Formula One (F1) calendar.
Speaking to Sky Sports commentator Martin Brundle during a live pre-race grid walk at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC), Anwar said this was being looked into.
"Well, I'm looking forward to it. We are discussing," he said in a brief reply to Brundle.
Anwar, who was soaked after heavy rain drenched the circuit earlier, said he was nevertheless excited by the return of F1 action to Sepang.
"Oh yes. You see, I'm wet, drenched, but excited. You see, the entire country is rejoicing," he said.
Meanwhile, in a social media post, Anwar said he earlier toured the SIC's G Hillstand to meet racing fans.
He praised the lively atmosphere and the Karnival Litar Rasa Madani, which featured around 40 local traders selling meals, drinks and snacks.
"Credit also to the Cooperatives and Entrepreneur Development Cooperation, Youth and Sports Ministry as well as all agencies involved in making this carnival a success, thus ensuring that the F1's festivities also lead to benefits for our local traders," he said.
The F1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia marks the return of the sport to Sepang after a nine-year absence, with the circuit last hosting an F1 race in 2017.
The 2026 event, held from Oct 2 to 4, was relocated from Bahrain to Sepang following an agreement involving the Malaysian and Bahrain governments, F1 and the FIA.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MARC Ratings raises red flag over Zetrix AI's governance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MARC Ratings has revised the MARCWatch status on Zetrix AI Bhd to "Negative" from "Developing", citing growing concerns over the company's transparency and governance.
The rating agency said it still lacked key information to assess the company's credit profile despite repeated requests.
This includes details on the substantial increase in borrowings and the allocation and utilisation of sizeable development expenditure, MARC Ratings said in a statement.
Its concerns were compounded by the resignation of Zetrix AI's external auditor, reported payment arrears and the suspension of certain operations.
Zetrix AI's Islamic Medium-Term Notes Programme of up to RM2 billion was rated AA-IS before the company was first placed on MARCWatch in September.
MARC Ratings said the revision to MARCWatch Negative reflected an increased likelihood of a rating downgrade.
"The MARCWatch status will remain in place pending the receipt of sufficient information and satisfactory clarification of the issues identified.
"Should the required information continue to be unavailable, or prove inadequate to support a reliable credit assessment, MARC Ratings may suspend the rating and subsequently withdraw it," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Woman killed, man injured as car crashes into road barrier
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: A 28-year-old woman was killed when the car she were travelling in crashed into a road barrier along the Kota Iskandar highway here, today.
A 27-year-old man in the vehicle sustained minor injuries in the incident.
It is yet to be determined who was the driver.
Johor Fire and Rescue Department operation commander Saifulnizam Salleh said seven rescuers were deployed to the scene following the 10.54am distress call.
Upon arriving they found the car had veered off the highway near a new development project along Jalan Bukit Indah-Puteri Harbour before crashing into the barrier.
The woman was pronounced dead at the scene by an accompanying medical assistant, while the man was rushed to the hospital.
The operation was brought under control at 12.36pm and concluded at 12.50pm.
Police are yet to release any details.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Loke to hold press conference tomorrow on MYEG, Zetrix suspension
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Transport Minister Anthony Loke will hold a press conference tomorrow morning on the Road Transport Department's (RTD) suspension of My E.G. Sdn Bhd and Zetrix AI Bhd as collection agents.
The press conference will take place at the Transport Ministry in Putrajaya at 11am.
On Friday, the RTD announced that the services of My E.G. Sdn Bhd and Zetrix AI Bhd as collection agents would be suspended effective Oct 5.
Both companies are under the MYEG Group.
The suspension followed reports that Zetrix AI owes the government more than RM200 million in unremitted collections from traffic summonses, road tax and driving licence renewals dating back to May 2023.
Yesterday, Malaysia Corruption Watch called on Putrajaya to explain how the two companies failed to remit up to RM200 million in revenue collected on behalf of the RTD.
Calling for an audit, the anti-corruption watchdog said money collected on behalf of the government must have a clear audit trail from the point of payment until the funds reach government accounts.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 52 foreigners detained in late-night raids on seven KL entertainment outlets
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Immigration officers detained 52 foreigners in late-night raids on seven entertainment outlets in the Dang Wangi area.
The Kuala Lumpur Immigration Department said the operation, dubbed Op Gegar, began at 1.30am and involved 74 of its enforcement officers, supported by 18 from the department's Special Tactical Force (Pastak).
The raids were carried out following intelligence gathering and public tip-offs about the presence of foreigners suspected of working illegally and abusing their visit passes.
In a post on its official Facebook page, the Kuala Lumpur Immigration Department said 170 people were screened during the operation.
"Of these, 52 foreigners, comprising 23 men and 29 women, were detained for various suspected immigration offences.
"The department also issued five Form 29 notices, or summonses to witnesses, to representatives of the premises to assist investigations," it said.
It added that the detainees are being investigated for various offences under the Immigration Act 1959/63, Passport Act 1966 and Immigration Regulations 1963.
"Among the suspected offences were not possessing valid travel documents, overstaying and violating the conditions of their passes.
"All detainees were taken to the Bukit Jalil Immigration depot for documentation and further investigation," it said.
Kuala Lumpur Immigration director Datuk Hamsha Injau said the enforcement operations would be intensified to ensure compliance with the country's immigration laws.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: India police investigate sexual harassment allegations during protests
Article:
NEW DELHI: Indian police launched an investigation on Sunday into allegations of sexual harassment against officers during protests in the capital against the country's election commission.
Protests began on Friday demanding the Election Commission of India (ECI) chief Gyanesh Kumar step down, alleging wrongdoing during a large-scale voter-roll revision that has struck millions of names from the lists.
The ECI has rejected allegations of wrongdoing. Kumar himself has not commented.
The harassment allegations were made on Saturday when police detained scores of protestors around the government-designated protest site of Jantar Mantar in New Delhi.
"Allegations of sexual harassment were made by three female journalists against police officers," Delhi police said in a statement, promising "a fair and impartial enquiry."
In a video posted on social media, a complainant said that a police officer pushed and touched her "inappropriately."
A third day of protests is slated in the capital on Sunday, including by left-wing groups and supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) – which began in May as a satirical online movement, succeeding in its campaign to oust the then education minister.
CJP chief Abhijeet Dipke, who warned against a police crackdown and detentions on Saturday, said that the accused officer "must be arrested immediately."
Neha Bora, an activist from a left-wing student organisation, called for protesters to march to New Delhi's central India Gate.
"From Streets to Protests, Women Are NOT SAFE!," she said in a post on social media.
Opposition politicians have accused the ECI of acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
They have said they will march to the Election Commission in New Delhi on Tuesday, and hold "Save Democracy" rallies countrywide afterwards.
The CJP has called for a "massive mobilisation of young Indians" in New Delhi on Oct 10.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Empty nets in Latin America as fish flee El Nino
Article:
FISHERMEN along Latin America's Pacific coast are reeling in half-empty nets as ocean warming aggravated by El Nino causes tuna, anchovies and other top catches to migrate to cooler waters.
From Ecuador and Peru in South America, to Panama and Guatemala in Central America, some skippers have stopped going out altogether as fish stocks dwindle close to shore, in seas running at up to six degrees Celsius above normal.
"The water is warm," Juan Ollague, 56, told AFP in the southwestern Ecuadoran port of Santa Rosa where hundreds of idle fishing boats are crammed into a small port.
After a night on the water, Ollague returns with just six small tuna.
"We came away empty-handed," he lamented.
"Fishing used to be good, now it's terrible," fellow skipper Darwin Zambrano, 53, complained as he untangled a net that hasn't scooped up big tuna like albacore or bonito in weeks.
El Nino is the warming phase of a natural cycle in the tropical Pacific that causes hotter and drier conditions in some places, and cooler and wetter in others.
This year's "super" El Nino, which is expected to peak later this year, is already wreaking havoc in Central America, where drought is endangering animals and stunting crops.
The average sea surface temperature, excluding polar regions, reached 21.07C in August, tying with March 2024 as the hottest on record, according to the European Union's Copernicus climage change observatory.
The average sea temperatures off Ecuador's coast rose by 2.5-3C at the surface and up to 6C at a depth of 40 metres in the past 10 weeks, said oceanographer Jonathan Cedeno, who led a mission from Guayaquil's Polytechnic University to measure the temperatures.
On Panama's Pacific coast, Rigoberto Gonzalez said he has to sail further and further from shore to earn a living.
This means spending more on food, ice to preserve the fish, and fuel for the small boat he uses to catch snapper, kingfish and barracuda.
"We go out with US$100 worth of gas, and when we come back, we earn US$150" from sales of the fish, which has to be divided among four workers, Gonzalez, 59, told AFP, on Veracruz beach.
[[nid:1547545]]
In nearby Panama City, some fishermen have thrown in the towel and decided to remain in port.
"We can't keep losing money," Jesus Morales, leader of the artisanal fishermen's union of Panama, said.
Further north, in Iztapa, Guatemala, 50-year-old Eliseo Ovando said it now takes three days to catch what he used to pull from the water in a day, and complains that only commercial fisheries receive government assistance to ride out the shortages.
"The big fish eat the little ones," he said, referring to the struggles of small-scale operators like himself.
In Peru, the world's biggest catcher of anchovies, fishermen are turning to construction to feed their families as their tiny prey slips out of reach.
In Panama City, the poor yields are visible at a wholesale fish market next to the dock that supplies the city's supermarkets.
"Less is arriving" off the boats, says Carlos Nieto, a 46-year-old vendor. And sometimes the catch is "damaged by the heat," he said.
Nieto now spends about $600 a month on ice, "practically a whole salary."
For now, vendors in Panama haven't passed on their higher costs and reduced income to consumers in the form of significantly higher prices.
But in Ecuador, the world's second-largest tuna producer after Thailand, the prices of mahi-mahi (also known as dorado) and swordfish have doubled due to the shortage, according to the industry.
In Santa Rosa, the sea's dwindling bounty has a knock-on effect, leading to the temporary closure of food stalls along the port.
Francisco Orlando, who earns a living filleting fish, is worried that he could soon be out of a job.
"We're hoping they (fishermen) catch fish," the 37-year-old explained as he sharpened his knives to separate the bones from the meat.
"If they do, we work. If they don't, we don't."
* The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 4, including baby girl, killed in East-West Highway crash [WATCH]
Article:
GERIK: Four people, including a baby girl, were killed in a three-vehicle collision along the East-West Highway (JRTB) from Kelantan towards Gerik here today.
The victims comprised two men, a woman and a baby girl.
Gerik Fire and Rescue Station chief Mohd Rais Mahmud said the department received a distress call about the accident at 12.56pm.
He said firefighters rushed to the scene and found that the accident involved a lorry and two cars.
"Four victims travelling in a Perodua Axia were confirmed dead at the scene, while a boy was injured.
"The bodies were handed over to the police for further action, while the injured boy was taken to hospital for treatment," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Russia strikes hit Kyiv as Germany's Merz visits
Article:
KYIV: Russia struck a bridge in Kyiv on Sunday soon after Germany's chancellor arrived in Ukraine's capital on a surprise visit to demonstrate European support in the face of an upsurge in attacks.
Air raid sirens blared across Kyiv, urging residents to shelter, soon after Friedrich Merz's arrival under tight security, with warnings of approaching Russian attack drones.
Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko then confirmed that a strike had damaged the road surface on the Northern Bridge – one of several connecting the eastern and western parts of the city over the Dnipro river which have been struck in recent days.
Images posted on messaging channels appeared to show a missile slamming into the structure, sending a fireball into the air.
Klitschko has said that Kyiv – largely spared from the devastation wrought near the frontlines in nearly five years of conflict – should now be on a war footing due to the upsurge in attacks.
A spate of round-the-clock attacks has hit residential areas, petrol stations, schools, rail and communications infrastructure.
Merz said the country "needs all our support in the coming weeks."
"If Russia is not stopped, its war machine will sooner or later turn against us," he added.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has repeatedly urged Ukraine's Western allies for more military support, including advanced interceptors to shoot down Russia's new fast-moving, jet-powered drones.
Merz and Zelenskyy were due to meet and government sources in Berlin said they were expected to agree a new package of military support worth more than $1 billion.
It includes combat drones and satellite technology to help Ukraine hit Russian launch sites, as well as for the joint production of anti-jet drones, the German sources said.
"This support addresses the most significant current gap in Ukraine's air defence system. The impact is expected to be rapid and tangible," a source said.
Merz this week called for unity against Russia within Nato and the European Union as well as his own country, where the far-right, Moscow-friendly AfD opposition is on the rise.
There have been increasing fears in Europe that it could find itself in Russia's crosshairs, including from covert attacks, if it is not stopped in Ukraine.
On Saturday, Russia warned foreigners and diplomats to leave Kyiv, saying "massive" new airstrikes would hit the city.
The Russian foreign ministry declared in a statement that "responsibility for any potential negative consequences rests entirely with those who ignore this warning."
Moscow had issued a similar warning in May, but leaders from countries supporting Ukraine have defied the Russian warnings and continued to make visits.
"The EU Delegation is staying. Threatening us will not stop Europe's support for Ukraine. It only reminds us why that support matters!" EU ambassador Katarina Mathernova wrote on X on Sunday.
Mathernova told AFP separately that "nobody is moving", although European embassies always had contingency plans, including for winter, she added.
Russia has admitted deliberately targeting Ukraine's energy sector as winter approaches. Last year, similar attacks knocked out power and heating for days on end as temperatures plummeted to -20C.
In Kyiv, which is home to some three million people, residents have begun mulling what to do if that happens again.
The government has also suggested that the vulnerable and disabled should consider leaving.
Merz's trip was expected to announce some 350 million euros to help provide generators, transformer stations and for grid repairs, German government sources said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iran FM tells US there is no military solution to their conflict
Article:
TEHERAN: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Sunday that there was no military solution to his country's conflict with the United States, with talks on ending the war apparently at an impasse.
A campaign of heavy bombardment failed to bring a decisive close to the war launched by the US and Israel in late February, and Washington in recent weeks has dialled back military operations in favour of economic pressure.
"If our enemies again choose the path of military confrontation, our response will be stronger than before, and we will defend ourselves with even more force," Araghchi said at a gathering of foreign ambassadors.
"There is no military solution, nor any solution based on new sanctions," he continued, adding "only negotiations based on justice and fairness" could end the conflict.
The two sides agreed a memorandum of understanding in June aimed at providing a framework for a permanent resolution, but the deal collapsed, largely due to disagreements over the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran has sought to impose control over the vital shipping lane since the start of the war, and has attacked vessels that attempt to transit without its authorisation.
Iranian and US officials last week held indirect talks on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, with Tehran saying it presented seven conditions for reopening the strait.
Trump, however, rejected the proposal, while leaving the door open both to further talks or renewed military operations.
The United States has not struck Iran since Sept 1.
US media outlet Axios reported that top Trump cabinet members met Friday to discuss the war in Iran, as well as the conflict in Yemen, where the Teheran-backed Houthis have been fighting government forces and attacking Saudi Arabia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mubarak: Melaka election may indicate whether GE16 will be called early
Article:
KUANTAN: The upcoming Melaka election could serve as an indicator of whether the 16th General Election (GE16) will be called earlier, said the Council of Former Elected Representatives (Mubarak).
Its president, Tan Sri Abdul Aziz Abdul Rahman, said the current political momentum and Barisan Nasional's strength could be factors influencing the timing of the next general election.
"GE16 needs to be held sooner, given BN's current strength. However, we will have to see what happens in Melaka... the Melaka election will serve as an indicator of the timing of GE16.
"If BN walks away with a victory, then the general election could be pushed back until the end of the term," he told reporters after Mubarak's 23rd annual general meeting here.
BN secured victories in the Johor and Negri Sembilan elections held this year and is looking to retain Melaka, where it won 21 out of 28 seats in the previous state election.
The Election Commission is scheduled to meet on Oct 7 to decide on the nomination and polling dates for the Melaka election.
On the possibility of cooperation between Umno and Pas in GE16, Aziz said it would ultimately be a "game of numbers", with both parties needing to assess their respective strengths and field winnable candidates.
"If Umno and Pas can work together and combine their strengths, then go ahead. Once you are already in power, you can decide who you want to bring in (parties to work together with)," he said.
Meanwhile, he said it was high time for the country to create three deputy prime minister posts, with one each representing Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak.
"Sabah and Sarawak are quite financially independent and have a lot of resources, so it is not proper to leave them out of the mainstream administration.
"This move is to create inclusiveness and a sense of collective leadership, rather than having the administration dominated by leaders from Peninsular Malaysia," he said.
Malaysia currently has two deputy prime ministers — Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof.
Fadillah is the first deputy prime minister from East Malaysia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: King attends F1 Bahrain Grand Prix at SIC
Article:
SEPANG: The return of Formula 1 to the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) after a nine-year absence received special attention today when His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, attended the 2026 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix F1 race, together with the top leaders of Malaysia, Bahrain and Brunei.
His Majesty was received on arrival at about 2.15pm by Bahrain Crown Prince sand Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Also attending the race were the Sultan of Brunei, Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah, and Prince Abdul Mateen Bolkiah, who were received by Anwar at about 2.35pm.
The Raja Muda of Selangor, Tengku Amir Shah Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah; the Tunku Mahkota of Kedah, Tunku Shazuddin Ariff Sultan Sallehuddin; and the Tengku Mahkota of Kelantan, Tengku Muhammad Fakhry Petra; also attended the race, marking the return of the roar of F1 engines to Sepang after the last race was held there in 2017.
The race, scheduled to start at 3 pm, was slightly delayed due to heavy rain after Negaraku and the Bahrain national anthem were played.
The event is expected to attract nearly 100,000 spectators and will also feature a fly-past by Gulf Air aircraft before the race gets underway.
Four-time world champion Max Verstappen of Red Bull Racing will start the 56-lap race from pole position, followed by seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton of Ferrari and current championship leader Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes-AMG Petronas.
In July, F1 confirmed Malaysia as the host venue for the Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix from Oct 2 to 4, following an agreement between Formula 1, the Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA), and the Malaysian and Bahraini governments.
F1's return to Malaysia followed discussions and cooperation involving His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim and Bahrain's King Hamad bin Isa Al-Khalifa, as well as the two governments, to retain the Bahrain Grand Prix on the 2026 F1 calendar after the race was cancelled earlier this season due to geopolitical tensions in West Asia.
Malaysia previously hosted the Malaysian Grand Prix at SIC from 1999 to 2017 before the race was dropped from the F1 calendar. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Loke says resignation timing agreed with Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said the timing of his resignation, which will take effect once former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak pays the RM50 million fine, was agreed with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim when he tendered his resignation.
"Of course, people say that it's an act, political, and so on. But I'm sticking my head out — the moment he returns, I have to quit. I am not wishy-washy or dilly-dally. He goes home. I leave," said Loke, who is the transport minister, in an interview with The Straits Times.
Loke
announced
on Sept 19 that he would quit the Cabinet in protest against Najib being allowed to serve the remainder of his graft sentence under house arrest, following the Pardons Board's decision to grant him the arrangement.
Loke said his decision illustrated the balancing act between staying in power and holding to principles that the party says it cannot abandon.
He submitted his resignation to Anwar on Sept 28.
However, his clarification on Sept 29 that
his resignation
would only take effect once Najib pays the RM50 million fine drew criticism.
On Sept 18, Najib was
granted house arrest
for the remainder of his sentence, subject to his paying the RM50 million fine imposed following his conviction in the SRC International case.
Meanwhile, in the interview, the Seremban MP acknowledged that while DAP continues to command strong support among Chinese voters, this alone is insufficient to deliver federal power, with growing disappointment among its core electorate remaining a concern.
Loke said DAP would never take Chinese support "for granted", but added that the party must build consensus with its coalition partners.
"We know sometimes it's frustrating to be in this kind of situation, but that is the reality of Malaysian politics.
"There is no way for DAP to form a government on its own without working with others.
This is a reality we must accept: We can only push as far as possible, relying on objective and persuasive arguments to get things done within the system," he said.
That pragmatism also extends to DAP's potential partners after the 16th General Election, with Loke saying the party's door remains open despite opposition among some grassroots members to parties such as Pas, Umno and Bersatu.
He pointed to DAP's decision to work with Umno after the 2022 general election to form the Anwar-led federal government as evidence that political alliances can shift according to circumstances.
"I don't close my doors to anyone. I hold this belief that we have come to a point that politics has to be agile.
"Of course, not without any principle or any precondition, because it depends on the circumstances what is best for the country to move forward."
Loke also remained confident that the Malay unity narrative promoted by Umno and Pas would not be sustainable.
"Negeri Sembilan's defeat is basically a blessing in disguise for us. They (Umno-Pas) talked about Malay unity and forming a formidable state government to resolve the royal impasse. What decision did they make? They dethroned the state ruler.
"Right now, Malays elsewhere in the entire country can see that an Umno-Pas government did this.
"So that's why I said DAP is being spared this burden right now. In a way, the Malay unity momentum cannot necessarily be sustained in terms of electoral trends."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sabah gives more than 500 adults second chance to learn reading, writing, counting
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 4 — More than 500 adults in Sabah who missed out on formal education are being given a second chance to master basic reading, writing and counting (3M) skills through the Functional Literacy Education Programme (PLF) organised by the Community Development Department (KEMAS).
Sabah KEMAS director Ahmad Fakhrul Azman Muhammad Radzi said the participants are attending 25 classes this year in urban fringe, rural and remote areas across Kudat, Kota Marudu, Kota Belud, Keningau, Tenom, Nabawan, Beluran, Sandakan, Kinabatangan, Lahad Datu, Semporna, Tawau and Kalabakan.
The programme primarily targets individuals aged between 15 and 65 who have yet to master basic 3M skills, while those outside the age range can also participate based on their needs.
“PLF is among the efforts to eradicate illiteracy, particularly among those who dropped out of formal education at an early stage and are still unable to read, write and count,” he told Bernama.
Participants are identified with the help of community leaders, including village heads, as well as KEMAS teachers on the ground, who provide information on individuals still in need of literacy education.
Before joining the classes, participants sit for a pre-test to assess their initial reading, writing and counting skills. A post-test is conducted upon completion to measure their progress, with more than 70 per cent recorded as achieving an excellent level.
Those who have yet to fully master the three skills can repeat the lessons to ensure they reach the required level.
Ahmad Fakhrul said regular PLF classes run for a year and are conducted by KEMAS-appointed PLF community development officers who serve as trained educators in the targeted areas.
Classes conducted by additional instructors in areas with greater needs run for six months, with three sessions a week.
As part of efforts to recognise participants and encourage them to continue learning, graduation ceremonies are held according to class and district.
A total of 375 participants from 25 classes took part in this year’s ceremonies, which were conducted by groups and according to their respective districts.
“Participants who complete the programme receive certificates as recognition and encouragement to continue learning. We do not know whether they may eventually become interested in pursuing further education,” he said.
Beyond literacy, KEMAS instructors also expose participants to livelihood and entrepreneurship skills through the production of items such as handicrafts, fish crackers and rempeyek, based on local needs.
“We want participants to apply their basic 3M skills in small-scale entrepreneurship so that they can indirectly generate income,” said Ahmad Fakhrul.
As technology advances, PLF participants are also introduced to digital skills to help them keep pace with current developments and reduce the digital divide.
They are guided in using smartphones for everyday tasks, including making clinic appointments through the MySejahtera application and paying bills, as well as promoting their products online
“Efforts to eradicate illiteracy must continue and receive support from all parties so that no one, particularly in Sabah, is left behind in education.
“We do not want them to be easily deceived in their daily affairs because of literacy limitations. Instead, they should be supported until they can become independent and live their lives with greater confidence,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: F1 excitement at Sepang also brings opportunities for local traders
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — The return of Formula 1 (F1) to the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) after a nine-year absence has not only delighted motorsport fans but also provided an opportunity for about 40 local traders to earn an income through the Karnival Litar Rasa Madani.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the carnival, held at the G Hillstand at SIC in conjunction with the 2026 F1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP), brought together local traders offering a variety of food and beverages, including snacks and light refreshments.
He said that the lively atmosphere at the circuit also gave visitors an opportunity to enjoy local fare while watching the race and, at the same time, supporting local traders.
“I took the opportunity to visit the G Hillstand at the Sepang International Circuit, which accommodates most of the Madani ticket holders, while meeting F1 fans.
“The atmosphere here is lively, with an interesting view of the circuit as well as the Karnival Litar Rasa Madani While enjoying the race at the circuit, visitors can also enjoy a meal and support our traders!” Anwar said in a Facebook post today.
The Prime Minister added that the organisation of the Karnival Litar Rasa Madani was one of the efforts to ensure that the excitement surrounding F1 also generated economic benefits for local traders.
“My appreciation to the Ministry of Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives (KUSKOP), the Ministry of Youth and Sports (KBS) and all agencies involved in making this carnival a success, thereby ensuring that the excitement surrounding F1 also brings greater opportunities for local traders,” he said.
In July, F1 confirmed Malaysia as the host of the Gulf Air Bahrain GP, from Oct 2 to 4, following an agreement between Formula 1, the Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA), and the governments of Malaysia and Bahrain.
The return of F1 to Malaysia followed discussions and cooperation involving His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and King of Bahrain, King Hamad bin Isa Al-Khalifa; as well as the two governments, to retain the Bahrain GP on the 2026 F1 calendar, after the race was cancelled earlier this season due to geopolitical tensions in West Asia.
Malaysia previously hosted the Malaysian GP at SIC from 1999 to 2017, before being dropped from the F1 calendar. — Bernama

Title: Zahid urges UiTM to establish Quantum Department, says Malaysia must not lag
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 4 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has called on Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) to establish a Quantum Department to ensure the country does not lag behind current advancements.
He said the department is targeted to be established next year to ensure local expertise can be developed at an early stage.
“AI is indeed good and is being implemented very well, but quantum is a new technology based on the latest technological developments, and Malaysia should not lag behind in this area.
“I am very confident that its potential is immense in attracting many students to pursue studies in this field and eventually, in less than a decade, producing quantum experts in our country,” he said.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also the Rural and Regional Development Minister, said this after officiating the ‘Wacana Semarak Patriotisme: Seminar Ilmuwan Islam’ at the university’s Dewan Agung Tuanku Canselor here today.
Quantum technology is an advanced field of science and engineering that harnesses properties of quantum mechanics, such as superposition and entanglement of subatomic particles, to process information at extraordinary speeds.
Ahmad Zahid said his ministry would also contribute RM500,000 to UiTM to support the development of programmes such as the TVET UiTM Dihatiku training and certification programme and UTAMA PLUS UiTM AI Certified, including the development of the Quantum Department. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia eyes F1 calendar return as PM Anwar confirms talks under way
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Malaysia is discussing a possible return to the Formula One calendar beyond this weekend’s race at Sepang, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today, raising hopes of a longer-term revival of the Malaysian Grand Prix.
Anwar confirmed the talks during a brief exchange with Sky Sports commentator Martin Brundle on the grid at the Sepang International Circuit ahead of today’s Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.
Asked by Brundle about the prospect of Malaysia returning to the F1 calendar in future, Anwar replied: “Well, I’m looking forward to it. We are discussing.”
The remark is the clearest indication yet that Putrajaya is considering extending Malaysia’s renewed association with Formula One beyond this weekend, which marked the sport’s first race at Sepang in nine years.
Drenched after heavy rain swept across the circuit and delayed the start, Anwar nevertheless said the mood surrounding Formula One’s return had been overwhelmingly positive.
“Oh yes. You see, I’m wet, drenched, but excited. You see, the entire country is rejoicing,” he told Brundle.
Formula One returned to Sepang this weekend for the first time since 2017 after the Bahrain Grand Prix was relocated to Malaysia because of security concerns linked to conflict in the Middle East.
The October 2-4 race retained its official Bahrain Grand Prix designation and was arranged as a one-off event.
Malaysia previously hosted a Formula One race annually from 1999 until 2017, when the government ended the event amid concerns over high costs and diminishing returns.
The economics of a permanent comeback remain a major hurdle.
Sepang International Circuit chief executive Azhan Shafriman Hanif has said Malaysia would require at least RM300 million a year to secure a regular place on the F1 calendar, with any return also dependent on a slot becoming available.
By contrast, Malaysia’s expenditure for this weekend’s event was estimated at between RM10 million and RM16 million because Bahrain had already borne the major hosting costs.

Title: Brunei Sultan departs after witnessing F1 Gulf Air Bahrain GP return to Sepang
Article:
SEPANG, Oct 4 — The Sultan of Brunei, Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah, departed for home today after concluding his special visit in conjunction with the Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP) at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC).
The aircraft carrying His Majesty and the Brunei delegation, including Prince Abdul Mateen Bolkiah, took off at 5.30 pm after a red carpet send-off, which included a guard of honour mounted by 28 officers and personnel from the First Battalion of the Royal Malay Regiment.
Minister of Youth and Sports Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari, Brunei High Commissioner to Malaysia Dato Paduka Abdu’r Rahmani Basir and Chief of Protocol Ambassador Mohd Ikram Ibrahim were present at the Bunga Raya Complex here to bid farewell to His Majesty and his delegation.
Earlier, Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah attended the F1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at SIC with His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and the top leaders of Malaysia, Bahrain and Brunei to witness the return of the prestigious F1 race to Sepang after a nine-year absence.
Also attending the race were Bahrain Crown Prince and Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
In July, F1 confirmed Malaysia as the host venue for the Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix from Oct 2 to 4, following an agreement between Formula 1, the Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA), and the governments of Malaysia and Bahrain.
F1’s return to Malaysia followed discussions and cooperation involving His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim and Bahrain’s King Hamad Isa Al-Khalifa, as well as the two governments, to retain the Bahrain Grand Prix on the 2026 F1 calendar after the race was cancelled earlier this season due to geopolitical tensions in West Asia.
Malaysia previously hosted the Malaysian Grand Prix at SIC from 1999 to 2017 before being dropped from the F1 calendar. — Bernama

Title: Boy mauled by pack of five stray dogs in Bachok receives rabies jab, shows signs of recovery
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Oct 4 — An eight-year-old boy who was seriously injured after being attacked by a pack of stray dogs at Pantai Kuala Kemasin, Bachok, on Thursday has received a rabies vaccination and is now being monitored for three weeks.
The boy’s mother, Rosnani Mat Salleh, 46, said her son, Azuar Firdaus Zuraiman, showed positive progress today after remaining withdrawn for two days as he was still traumatised by the incident.
“For two days after the incident, he was still frightened and did not want to talk. He mostly kept to himself and sometimes cried because he was in pain from his injuries, especially to his head and neck.
“Thankfully, his condition has improved today and he has started talking. He can now answer when asked and can recount what happened during the incident,” she told reporters at Raja Perempuan Zainab II Hospital here today.
Earlier, Rosnani and her son were visited by the Kelantan Education Department (JPN) Student Development Sector deputy director, Norazan Mat Nor.
Recalling the incident, Rosnani said Azuar Firdaus was playing on the beach around 9.30 am with three relatives when five stray dogs approached.
She said the three relatives, aged between two and 11, managed to run away, but Azuar Firdaus fell while trying to escape and became the dogs’ target.
“He tried to escape by running into the sea, but the dogs continued chasing him until someone came to his aid and rescued him. He was semi-conscious after the incident and suffered injuries to his head, neck and hand, including bite wounds, in addition to scratches on his back,” she said.
Rosnani said her son underwent a five-hour surgery the day after the incident to treat his injuries.
She said Azuar Firdaus also received a rabies vaccination and is expected to continue being monitored for about three weeks.
Meanwhile, Norazan said the department is aware of the incident, which is believed to be the first involving a student being seriously injured in a stray dog attack.
He added that the victim has shown positive progress and is expected to be discharged from hospital today. — Bernama

Title: Amanah says Pakatan open to partners to form stable Melaka govt ahead of state election
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 4  — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is open to seeking allies to form a stable government in Melaka in the upcoming state election, said Amanah secretary-general Muhammad Faiz Fadzil.
He said Amanah’s stand was that it was better for the coalition to find partners who could work together to form a stable state government.
Muhammad Faiz said a decision on possible cooperation was expected to be made soon but the possibility of PH contesting on its own remained open.
“Amanah believes that joining forces with allies who want to establish a stable government in Melaka would be better,” he told reporters after the LKIM chairman’s engagement session with Telok Mas fishermen at the Tanjong Nibong fishermen’s jetty here today.
Muhammad Faiz said any decision on political cooperation would be determined by the PH Presidential Council, but Amanah had been exploring collaboration with various parties.
In the 2021 state election, Barisan Nasional won 21 of the 28 seats contested, while PH took five and Perikatan Nasional two.
The Election Commission is meeting on Wednesday to set the dates for the state polls. — Bernama

Title: Negeri Sembilan joins Johor on unhealthy air list as haze lingers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — A total of eight locations recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in the unhealthy category as of 4pm today.
According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, five areas in Johor were affected, involving Segamat (156), Batu Pahat (155), Kluang (152), Tangkak (151) and Larkin (111).
In Negeri Sembilan, the affected areas were Nilai (151) and Seremban (146), while Samarahan, Sarawak, recorded a reading of 117.
Meanwhile, 57 areas were in the moderate category, while three areas recorded good readings.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and an API exceeding 300 hazardous. — Bernama

Title: Another woman files report against motivational speaker as Perlis police probe alleged sexual harassment
Article:
KANGAR, Oct 4 — Perlis police have confirmed receiving another report against a male motivational speaker over an allegation of sexual harassment.
Perlis police chief DCP Hamzah Hashim said the report was received yesterday and involved a 19-year-old female complainant.
“The case is being investigated under Section 509 of the Penal Code, Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998, and Section 14 of the Minor Offences Act,” he said in a statement today.
Hamzah said the man is currently under a two-day remand order ending today in connection with a police report lodged in Padang Besar.
He said the motivational speaker would be released on police bail before being re-arrested by Kangar police for further action.
He added that an application for remand to assist investigations into the Kangar case would be made at the Kangar Magistrates’ Court tomorrow. — Bernama

Title: F1 roars back at Sepang as Sultan Ibrahim, Bahrain and Brunei royals watch on
Article:
SEPANG, Oct 4 — The return of Formula 1 to the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) after a nine-year absence received special attention today when His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, attended the 2026 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix F1 race, together with the top leaders of Malaysia, Bahrain and Brunei.
His Majesty was received on arrival at about 2.15 pm by Bahrain Crown Prince and Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Also attending the race were the Sultan of Brunei, Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah, and Prince Abdul Mateen Bolkiah, who were received by Anwar at about 2.35 pm.
The Raja Muda of Selangor, Tengku Amir Shah Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah; the Tunku Mahkota of Kedah, Tunku Shazuddin Ariff Sultan Sallehuddin; and the Tengku Mahkota of Kelantan, Tengku Muhammad Fakhry Petra; also attended the race, marking the return of the roar of F1 engines to Sepang after the last race was held there in 2017.
The race, scheduled to start at 3 pm, was slightly delayed due to heavy rain after Negaraku and the Bahrain national anthem were played.
The event is expected to attract nearly 100,000 spectators and will also feature a fly-past by Gulf Air aircraft before the race gets underway.
Cars enter the pit lane after the start of theGulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix F1 race was delayed by heavy rain at the Sepang International Circuit on October 4, 2026, which marks F1’s return to Malaysia after a nine-year absence. — AFP pic
Four-time world champion Max Verstappen of Red Bull Racing will start the 56-lap race from pole position, followed by seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton of Ferrari and current championship leader Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes-AMG Petronas.
In July, F1 confirmed Malaysia as the host venue for the Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix from Oct 2 to 4, following an agreement between Formula 1, the Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA), and the Malaysian and Bahraini governments.
